newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah ends weaker on baht spillover.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah ends weaker on baht spillover.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah ended weaker against the dollar on Wednesday after a volatile day.
The rupiah strengthened to a high of 2,530 from an opening of 2,570/80 but fell back to 2,582/87 at the close.
Dealers said the rupiah was on the way to recovery before fresh pressure on the baht spilled over to the rupiah and other regional currencies and pushed rates lower against the dollar.

The rupiah was trapped in range trading throughout the day, with minor intervention by the central bank seen helping provide direction to the market, but new jolts in Thailand eroded Bank Indonesia's initiative.
Dealers said central bank intervention was seen at the 2,580 level which helped boost the rupiah to 2,540 level in late morning, but the baht slump weakened the rupiah.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,585.25/95.25 and 2,570.50/80.50, respectively.
"Sentiment has turned bearish on the rupiah after opening with bullish sentiment, with attempts to break the 2,500 resistance level," one U.S. bank dealer said.
A slump in the Thai baht seemed to have pulled the region down into another round of jittery although it was less rough.
One local bank dealer said the market remained volatile, reflected by a wide spread and perception that the turbulence was not over yet although the rupiah had recovered somewhat.
Dealers said the spillover triggered operators to buy swaps, whose rises were limited because the market had been long.
One-month swap was at 18.0/20.0, two at 37.0/42.0, three at 60.0/66.0 and six at 118.0/125.0 points.
"The tone is also biddish on longer-term swaps. But short-term swaps are cheap due to ample rupiah supply," one said. Overnight swap was at 0.1/0.3 and tom/next at -0.1/par.
Overnight rupiah closed at 13.0 percent after the central bank raised its one-to-two day bilateral papers (SBIs).
The central bank continued to keep short-term rates high to reduce speculative dollar buying using cheap rupiah.
Dealers said the bank raised overnight SBIs rates to 13.0 percent from 12.0 percent and that for two-week papers to eight percent from 7.5 percent.
The bank kept all other rates unchanged.
The bank offered five-to-six day SBIs at 12.0 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
One market analyst said there was still a lot of volatility in the market and it was difficult to read whether any move in the market was based on flows or real corporate orders.

One dealer said earlier if the rupiah could break the 2,500 resistance level, then there was potential for a strong comeback. But if it fell below the 2,600 level, speculators would launch an attack to test the band again.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,549/2,597 on Wednesday from 2,576/2,624 on Tuesday.
